_purpose: Authoritative declaration of what every model input IS and where it must come from. This is the specification; DATA_SOURCING_REGISTRY.json records what the current build actually holds. Divergence between the two is the work queue.
_method: CAPRI symbols are read from GDX dumps (gdxdump listing format), never from Excel exports. The Excel path produced homoglyph corruption, ragged vintages and dropped regional detail.

_status_values.GDX: sourced from a CAPRI GDX read, current
_status_values.GDX_PENDING: available in a dump already held, not yet wired
_status_values.GDX_NEEDED: requires a dump we do not have
_status_values.LITERATURE: correctly a published constant, not a CAPRI output
_status_values.EXTERNAL: belongs to another model or database, not CAPRI
_status_values.UNRESOLVED: definitional or mapping question, not an extraction problem

yields.csv.concept: output per hectare (crops) or per head (livestock)
yields.csv.note: Dairy yield is in COMI, not YILD. Taking YILD uniformly puts dairy 3x too low.

base_areas.csv.concept: activity levels in the base year
base_areas.csv.coverage: 78.9% by area, 3853 cells from DATA2 LEVL
base_areas.csv.note: COTT, OFIB and OFOD remain flat placeholders: CAPRI aggregates fibre as TEXT and fodder as OFAR/ROOF, which needs a documented split.

variable_costs.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 TOIN, or the sum of FERT SEED REPM REPB ELEC EGAS EFUL ELUB INPO IRRO CAOF
variable_costs.csv.note: TOIN is total intermediate input, marginally broader than 'variable cost'. Components sum to 67% of TOIN, so the remainder is items not itemised. PLAP must not be used: in these dumps it duplicates PESTOTAL, a quantity index.

producer_prices.csv.note: Must be merged together with variable_costs. The two were internally consistent only with each other; changing one alone puts staples at an implausible loss.

cap_payments.csv.concept: CAP premium per unit of activity
cap_payments.csv.note: Was region x instrument summed to 676.7 EUR/ha at DE11 and applied uniformly to all crops, nothing to livestock. CAPRI PRME is per activity: 360.8 soft wheat, 108.2 dairy cows, 8.2 bulls.

land_availability.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 LEVL on the aggregate activities ARAB, UAAR, GRAE, GRAI, SETA, FALL, OLND
land_availability.csv.note: GRAE and GRAI are identical in these dumps, so grassland maps to GRAE alone; summing would double-count.

animal_numbers.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 LEVL / HERD on animal activities
animal_numbers.csv.note: COWS and SHGO have no direct CAPRI counterpart and keep prior values.

nutrient_coefs.csv.note: Was national constants per activity. Real variation is large: soft wheat nitrogen 147.5 kg/ha in DE11 against 68.2 in ES61, where 125.9 was used everywhere.

manure_nutrients.note: New input. The hardcoded constants were wrong both ways: dairy understated 29% (85 vs 118.8), bulls overstated 49% (35 vs 23.5), laying hens absent where CAPRI has 659.5.

feed_requirements.csv.concept: energy, protein and dry matter requirement per head
feed_requirements.csv.unit: MJ NEL, kg CP, kg DM, days
feed_requirements.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 ENNE, CRPR, DRMN, DRMX, DAYS
feed_requirements.csv.note: reqrel_17*.gdx p_animReqCorrFac1 holds CORRECTION FACTORS, not levels. The levels are in DATA2.

supply_elasticities_regional.csv.note: The single largest remaining gap. Arable-only coverage drives the 7.97 asymmetry ratio that distorts every scenario. Needs the estnlp results dump.

pmp_crossgroup_terms.csv.note: 57% negative, i.e. genuine substitutes. The heuristic it replaced was uniformly positive.

input_requirements.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 SEED, FERT, PLAP, REPM, REPB, ELEC, EGAS, EFUL, ELUB
input_requirements.csv.note: Superseded in practice by the variable_costs merge from TOIN.

world_prices.csv.note: Validated via the producer/world arbitrage ratio using verified MPRI prices. Model retained for 7 commodities where CAPRI implies a domestic price below world; EGGS corrected from CAPRI (63.4 -> 1173.8).

armington_params.csv.capri_symbol: p_rhoArm1 / p_rhoArm2, literal in GAMS source
armington_params.csv.coverage: verified exact for 16 commodities; rho2 added for 21
armington_params.csv.note: No GDX or model run needed - the values are literal assignments in market1_ch.gms, included unconditionally by arm/market1.gms:165.

trade_flows_2021.csv.coverage: 547 region pairs x 32 commodities, 7468 records mapped
trade_flows_2021.csv.note: Recalibrated to 2017. The 2021 matrix it replaced had a ZERO DIAGONAL - all 29 self-trade pairs summed to exactly 0.0 - so the Armington first nest saw a 100% extra-EU import share for every commodity, including milk, pork and barley where intra-EU trade dominates. CAPRI 2017 gives milk 0.0%, pork 0.7%, barley 1.4%, wheat 3.1%, beef 6.5%, soya 89.9%. Median change 96.1 percentage points. Soya is the sanity check: it is genuinely almost entirely imported, and it is the one commodity the old matrix had nearly right by accident.

eu_mfn_tariffs.csv.note: Ultimately from TARIC/WTO. CAPRI carries a processed version; either is defensible if the year is declared.

climate_zones.csv.note: IPCC zone classification, not a CAPRI output.

crop_nutrient_export.csv.concept: nutrient removal per tonne of harvest
crop_nutrient_export.csv.note: CAPRI doc Table 15, reclassified from LITERATURE.

coco_feed_availability_national.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 FEED and the FCER/FGRA/FMAI/FPRO family
coco_feed_availability_national.csv.note: Regional, replacing national figures. 86888 source records.

pela_cross_price.note: Wired into the Q off-diagonals, taking precedence over the group-level p_pmpQuadPact. DE11 now has 118 negative off-diagonals; the previous heuristic was positive by construction.

market_supply_elasticities.note: EU medians wired into the market supply response.

livestock_output_coef.csv.concept: marketed product per head, by region and animal activity
livestock_output_coef.csv.capri_symbol: DATA2 COMI, BEEF, PORK, POUM, EGGS, SGMT, SGMI over elementary activities
livestock_output_coef.csv.note: Replaces YILD for livestock. CAPRI's YILD for breeding and suckler activities is not a marketed product - suckler cows carry 422.6 against 21.8 of beef - so gross_output built from it reported one region at 3.9 billion tonnes of pig. Built by tools/build_livestock_output_coef.py; EU totals match real 2017 production within 0.94-1.08 by product.

livestock_revenue_coef.csv.concept: market revenue per head, by region and animal activity
livestock_revenue_coef.csv.note: Used instead of price x YILD in livestock net revenue, for the same reason as the output coefficients. For crops MREV equals price x yield exactly (DE11 wheat: 135.6 x 6.15 = 833.7), which is what confirms it is the same concept. Dairy cow 2,771 EUR/head, laying hen 23.

nutrients_regional.csv.concept: mineral nitrogen applied per hectare, by region and crop
nutrients_regional.csv.note: CAPRI reports mineral (NMIN) and manure (NMAN) nitrogen separately per activity; their EU totals, 9.47 and 5.89 Mt, match the real ~10.8 and ~7. NITF is NOT an application rate - it equals NRET, a requirement. Regional rates matter: a single EU-wide table gave German regions EU-average fertilisation and a surplus of 14 kg N/ha where Germany's is among Europe's highest.

organic_yield_gap.csv.concept: organic vs conventional yield gap, by macro-region and product group
organic_yield_gap.csv.note: JRC Seville estimates from FADN data for the SUPREMA project; CAPRI loads them in gams/pol_input/greendeal/organic_area.gms rather than hard-coding them. Replaces a flat 20% assumption. The spread is the point: Southern Europe fruits -22.5% and olives -11.6%, Central Europe fruits -51.3% and cereals -42.9%. Reproduced in the report's Annex Table A3.3.

capri_own_price_elasticities.csv.concept: CAPRI's calibrated own-price supply elasticities, national market level
capri_own_price_elasticities.csv.note: REFERENCE DATA, not a model input: the supply model uses the REGIONAL PELA elasticities (supply_elasticities_regional.csv). These are national MARKET elasticities, a different quantity at a different aggregation - confusing the two once produced a false finding that annual crops were 0.14-0.51 of CAPRI. Kept because permanent crops and livestock vary only 1.0-1.6x across member states while annuals vary up to 141x, which is why per-country values matter for annuals.
gaps: wheat is absent from the parameter entirely; at market level it aggregates into WHEA

livestock_intensity_bounds.csv.note: CAPRI splits every dairy herd 50/50 between DCOL and DCOH in the base year, so the split carries no base-year information; the value is the response channel, letting dairy extensify under a nutrient target instead of only shrinking.

capri_ghg_mitigation.csv.concept: CAPRI mitigation technologies: shares, emissions under each technology, adoption costs
capri_ghg_mitigation.csv.note: CAPRI mitigation technologies: shares, emissions under each technology, adoption costs

capri_mitigation_potential.csv.concept: CAPRI technical mitigation potential by member state and source
capri_mitigation_potential.csv.note: CAPRI technical mitigation potential by member state and source

eu_gross_trade_supplement.csv.concept: CAPRI's extra-EU gross trade for commodities the trade file does not record (sugar, durum wheat)
eu_gross_trade_supplement.csv.note: Durum proxied from CAPRI WHEA flows scaled by durum share of wheat production; CAPRI trades wheat as one commodity.

land_rent_regional.csv.concept: Land rent per hectare by region (Eurostat apri_lrnt, arable land and/or permanent grassland)
land_rent_regional.csv.coverage: 209 of 248 regions from Eurostat (161 regional, 40 national, 8 arable-only national); 39 fallback
land_rent_regional.csv.note: Fallback for Germany and Cyprus: CAPRI 2030 accounts rent x median Eurostat/CAPRI ratio (0.41) - flagged in the source column; likely understates Germany.
gaps: Germany and Cyprus not published in apri_lrnt

capri_baseline_surplus_2030.csv.concept: CAPRI's own baseline gross N surplus per ha (2030 reference), input to the tiered nitrogen target
capri_baseline_surplus_2030.csv.coverage: 157 NUTS-2 direct, 82 scaled to national, 9 own
capri_baseline_surplus_2030.csv.note: Scenario-target input (vintage 2030, the scenario year), not base-year data.
gaps: regions split or merged between NUTS versions use national scaling

n_deposition_regional.csv.concept: Atmospheric N deposition per ha by region (CAPRI 2030 reference, EMEP-based)

manure_trade_2030.csv.concept: Manure N trade between regions: export share of excretion, import per ha of cropland

capri_fertiliser_allocation_2030.csv.concept: CAPRI fertiliser allocation per region and crop: need, mineral, manure, residues, losses (calibration data for the allocation module)

capri_regional_n_balance_2030.csv.concept: CAPRI regional N balance positions (MINFER, EXCRET, MTRADE, IMPORT, EXPPRD, CRESID, BIOFIX, ATMOSD, SURTOT)

fertiliser_substitution_2030.csv.concept: Manure-N availability and mineral-N efficiency per region (CAPRI fertiliser allocation): manure displaces mineral fertiliser at availability/efficiency

livestock_manure_n_coef.csv.concept: Manure N per head (kg), CAPRI 2017 regional manure N total per activity divided by this model's herd (census stock)
gaps: cells without CAPRI totals fall back to the previous per-unit table

livestock_feed_coef.csv.concept: Feed per head (t): cereals, protein-rich and energy-rich feed - CAPRI 2017 regional totals (FCER/FPRO/FENE x LEVL) divided by this model's herd
livestock_feed_coef.csv.note: Same construction as revenue and manure per head.
gaps: empty cells fall back to feed_requirements.csv

capri_oilseed_products_baseline.json.concept: Market balances of oilseed products (oils, cakes, seeds) by trade region; EU crushing and yields
capri_oilseed_products_baseline.json.note: Not yet read by the model (Stage 1 calibration data).

eu_demand_elas_overrides.json.concept: EU own-price demand elasticities for oils and cakes

feed_demand_nonEU.json.concept: Non-EU feed shares and feed-price elasticities

hardcoded_in_code._note: 277 numeric constants live in .py files, invisible to any data-file audit. Splitting them by whether they are legitimately constants matters more than the count.

environmental_module.py.note: IPCC emission factors and TAN fractions are published constants and belong in code. N_EXCRETION_KG_PER_HEAD is the exception: CAPRI computes it regionally as MANN.

capri_reference.py.note: NVZ nitrogen limits are legislation; IPCC factors are literature; CAPRI_RHOARM should come from the arm module.

feed_module.py.note: PRODUCTION_DAYS now overridden regionally. MEAN_LIVE_WEIGHT, FEED_MIN_SHARE and FEED_MAX_SHARE still hardcoded; CAPRI has p_minFeedShare and p_maxFeedShare.

loaders.py.note: NVZ_N_LIMITS_KG_HA duplicates CAPRI_NVZ_N_LIMITS in capri_reference.py. One of the two should go.
